item.title: From Wartime Operational Control to 'Conditions-Based Transition' – President Rhee's Letter (전작권, 이승만 대통령 편지에서 ‘조건에 기초한 전환’까지)
item.description:
The origins of the controversy surrounding the operational control (OPCON) of South Korean forces date back to the Korean War in 1950. (한국군의 작전통제권을 둘러싼 논란의 시작은 1950년 한국전쟁 때로 거슬러 올라간다.)

On July 14, 1950, President Syngman Rhee sent a letter to General Douglas MacArthur, commander of the United Nations Command (UNC), proposing the transfer of "command authority (now operational control) over the South Korean Army, Navy, and Air Force." General MacArthur accepted this in a reply on July 18, thereby transferring OPCON to the UNC. ( 1950년 7월14일 이승만 대통령은 더글러스 맥아더 유엔군사령관에게 편지를 보내 “한국 육군, 해군, 공군에 대한 지휘권(현 작전통제권)”을 이양할 것을 제안했다. 맥아더 사령관이 7월18일 답신에서 이를 수락하면서 작전권은 유엔군사령부(유엔사)로 넘어갔다.)

Shortly after the Korean War, in November 1954, South Korea and the United States stipulated in a bilateral agreed minutes that "as long as the UNC is responsible for the defense of the Republic of Korea, its forces shall be placed under the operational control of the UNC." ( 한·미는 한국전쟁 직후인 1954년 11월 체결한 한-미 합의의사록에서 “유엔사가 대한민국의 방위를 책임지는 한 그 군대를 유엔사의 작전통제권하에 둔다”고 규정했다. )

There were some changes to the OPCON exercised by the UNC in the 1960s. In September 1965, South Korea and the U.S. agreed that South Korean combat troops deployed to Vietnam would be released from UNC operational control and placed under South Korean command. Following the January 21 incident in 1968, when North Korean special forces attempted to raid the Blue House, South Korea's operational control over counter-infiltration operations was recognized in April of that year. (유엔사가 행사하던 작전권은 1960년대 일부 변화가 있었다. 한국과 미국은 1965년 9월 베트남에 파병된 한국군 전투병력은 유엔사 작전통제를 풀어 한국이 지휘하도록 했다. 1968년 북한군 특수부대가 청와대를 습격한 1·21사태 뒤에는 같은 해 4월 대간첩작전에 대한 한국의 작전통제권이 인정됐다.)

As national power grew and the Cold War eased in the late 1980s, South Korea's efforts to regain wartime operational control (Wartime OPCON) gained momentum. ( 1980년대 후반 들어 국력이 커지고 냉전이 누그러지자 한국의 전작권 환수 노력은 본격화했다.)

During the 1987 presidential election, candidate Roh Tae-woo of the Democratic Justice Party announced a pledge to "reclaim operational control." The Kim Young-sam administration regained only peacetime operational control in December 1994, citing the first North Korean nuclear crisis. In February 2007, the Roh Moo-hyun administration agreed with the U.S. to transfer Wartime OPCON to South Korea effective April 17, 2012. The date April 17 was chosen by reversing the date July 14, when former President Rhee had transferred OPCON. ( 1987년 대선 당시 노태우 민주정의당 후보는 “작전통제권을 환수하겠다”는 공약을 발표했고, 김영삼 정부는 1994년 12월 1차 북핵 위기 등을 이유로 평시작전통제권만 넘겨받았다. 노무현 정부는 2007년 2월 “2012년 4월17일부로 전시작전통제권(전작권)을 한국으로 이양한다”고 미국과 합의했다. 4월17일은 이승만 전 대통령이 전작권을 이양한 날짜인 7월14일을 거꾸로 한 택일이었다.)

However, the Lee Myung-bak administration postponed the transfer to December 1, 2015, citing unstable security conditions such as North Korea's second nuclear test (2009). The subsequent Park Geun-hye administration further delayed the transfer in April 2014, citing North Korea's third nuclear test. In particular, they agreed not to set a specific transfer date but to carry out the transition when mutually agreed conditions are met. The Moon Jae-in administration emphasized a "swift transfer of Wartime OPCON," but it did not materialize. Former President Yoon Suk Yeol showed little interest in reclaiming Wartime OPCON. (그러나 이명박 정부는 2010년 6월 북한의 2차 핵실험(2009년) 등 불안한 안보 상황을 들어 환수 시기를 2015년 12월1일로 늦췄고 이어 들어선 박근혜 정부는 2014년 4월 북한의 3차 핵실험 등을 이유로 환수를 연기했다. 특히 전작권 환수 시기를 특정하지 않고 양국이 상호 합의한 전환조건이 충족되는 시기에 전작권을 전환하기로 합의했다. 문재인 정부는 ‘조속한 전작권 전환’을 강조했지만 이뤄지지 않았다. 윤석열 전 대통령은 전작권 환수에 관심이 없었다.)

Amid these twists and turns, South Korea and the U.S. completed the first stage—Initial Operational Capability (IOC) assessment and verification for the future combined command that will replace the ROK-U.S. Combined Forces Command after the Wartime OPCON transfer—in 2019 and 2020, respectively. The second stage, Full Operational Capability (FOC) assessment, was completed in 2022, and verification is planned for the 58th ROK-U.S. Security Consultative Meeting this fall. After completing the third stage—Full Mission Capability (FMC) assessment and verification—the defense ministers of South Korea and the U.S. will recommend a transfer date to the two countries' presidents. The Lee Jae-myung administration hopes to reclaim Wartime OPCON by the end of 2027 at the earliest. The U.S. adopts a more cautious stance than South Korea. U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, attending the Asia Security Conference in Singapore on the 30th of last month, described the transfer of South Korea's Wartime OPCON as "encouraging" but emphasized the need to find a "balance" that respects U.S. military operational plans and responsibilities in the transition process. ( 이런 곡절 속에서 한·미는 전작권 환수 뒤 한미연합사를 대체할 미래연합사령부에 대해 1단계인 기본운용능력(IOC) 평가와 검증을 각각 2019년과 2020년 마쳤다. 2단계인 완전운용능력 평가는 2022년 마쳤고, 올해 가을 열리는 제58차 한·미 연례 안보협의회의에서 이를 검증할 계획이다. 한·미 국방장관은 3단계인 완전임무수행능력(FMC) 평가·검증까지 끝낸 뒤 한·미 대통령에게 전환 일자를 건의하게 된다. 이재명 정부는 이르면 2027년 말 전작권 환수를 바란다. 미국은 한국보다 신중한 태도다. 피트 헤그세스 미국 국방부 장관은 지난달 30일 싱가포르에서 열린 아시아안보회의에 참석해 한국의 전작권 전환을 두고 “고무적”이라고 평가하면서도 전환 과정에서는 미군의 작전 계획과 책임을 존중하는 ‘균형’을 찾아야 한다고 강조했다.)

By Kwon Hyuk-chul, Reporter nura@hani.co.kr ( 권혁철 기자 nura@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Few U.S. ground troops are deployed for initial combat on the Korean Peninsula in a contingency (한반도 유사시 초기 전투 투입되는 미국 지상군은 거의 없다)
item.description:
The Lee Jae-myung administration has pledged to retake wartime operational control (OPCON) and aims to complete this by as early as the end of 2027. President Lee expressed his resolve on the 19th, saying, "We are paying for our own defense, so why should the U.S. hold OPCON?" However, the U.S. side maintains that meeting conditions is a priority over timing, proposing a timeline of the first quarter of 2029 (as suggested by Lieutenant General Xavier Brunson, commander of the ROK-U.S. Combined Forces Command). Amid a temperature difference between South Korea and the U.S., there are voices domestically arguing that "the South Korean military still lacks capability." The Hankyoreh will examine the OPCON transfer issue in three installments, starting with the 6.25 War anniversary. (이재명 정부는 전시작전권 환수를 공약하고 빠르면 2027년 말까지 마무리하려 한다. 이 대통령은 지난 19일 “우리 돈 내며 방위를 책임질 건데, 전작권을 미국이 왜 갖고 있느냐”고 의지를 표명했다. 그러나 미국 쪽은 전작권 전환은 시기보다 조건 충족이 우선이라는 태도를 보이며 시기 역시 2029년 1분기(제이비어 브런슨 한미연합군사령관)를 제시했다. 한-미 간 온도 차가 있는 가운데 국내에서도 “한국군은 아직 능력이 부족하다”는 목소리가 있다. 한겨레는 6·25를 계기로 3회에 걸쳐 전작권 환수 쟁점을 짚어 본다.)

Defense Minister An Kyu-baek stated on the 26th of last month at the first Future National Defense Strategy Committee meeting attended by President Lee Jae-myung in Jinhae-gu, Changwon City, South Gyeongsang Province, "Even if wartime operational control (OPCON) is transferred tomorrow, there would be no major issue in defending ourselves." When President Lee responded, "It shouldn't be 'no major issue,' but rather 'no issue at all,'" Minister An replied, "No issue at all." The transfer of OPCON signifies recovering military sovereignty and possessing the capability to independently conduct war in times of crisis. <<> However, conservatives argue that "the South Korean military still lacks capability" and advocate for a 'cautious' transfer rather than a 'swift' one. They claim the South Korean military, compared to the U.S. military, is deficient in intelligence assets for monitoring North Korea, limited in precision strike capabilities, and lacks a command-and-control system. <<> Yet, among the combined ROK-U.S. forces deployed for the defense of South Korea in a contingency, there is almost no U.S. military power. <<> Ground forces are 99% South Korean. The navy is over 95% South Korean, and the air force is about 90% South Korean. This means that in a crisis on the Korean Peninsula, the South Korean military must assume most of the responsibility for the war. Currently, of the 28,500 U.S. troops stationed in South Korea, 18,000 are Army and 8,000 are Air Force. <<> In particular, U.S. forces in South Korea are not deployed for direct combat in the early stages of war. A government official said, "In the early stages of war, when casualties are high, a significant number of U.S. ground troops are assigned to evacuation operations for U.S. citizens," adding, "The U.S. military is continuously reducing its forces in the operational plans for the Korean Peninsula." <<> President Lee Jae-myung's confidence that "there would be no problem even if OPCON is transferred tomorrow" is based on his assessment that "the Republic of Korea has achieved defense capabilities stronger than at any time in history" (from his Armed Forces Day address last October). <<> According to data from Statistics Korea (now National Data Agency), North Korea's annual nominal GDP in 2024 was approximately 43.7 trillion won, while South Korea's defense budget for the same year was 59.4 trillion won. South Korea's defense spending exceeds the entire size of North Korea's national economy. The gap in defense spending between the two Koreas is estimated at $43.07 billion versus $1.604 billion, a 26-fold difference (2018, Stockholm International Peace Research Institute). North Korea allocates up to 15.8% of its total budget to defense, vowing to "continuously expand and strengthen self-reliant nuclear deterrence and war-fighting capabilities." However, realistically, South Korea's GDP is 59 times larger than North Korea's (as of 2024), making it difficult for the North to close the widening gap. <<> Since 2007, when OPCON transfer preparations began in earnest, the cumulative amount invested in pure force enhancement (excluding personnel costs, etc.) for the South Korean military stands at 176.3 trillion won. This funding has been primarily directed toward building intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) for real-time battlefield awareness, precision strike capabilities to immediately strike enemy strategic and tactical targets, and command-and-control (C2) capabilities for integrating all forces and information to make instantaneous decisions. These efforts have concentrated on strengthening the capabilities set as criteria in the conditional OPCON transfer agreement between South Korea and the U.S. in 2014: ISR, precision strike, and C2. <<> In the past, the South Korean military had to rely on U.S. intelligence assets like reconnaissance satellites and aircraft to track North Korean movements. Until the introduction of the Green Pine radar in 2012 for detecting ballistic missiles, South Korea didn't even know about North Korean ballistic missile launches unless the U.S. provided the information. Lacking an independent surveillance network against the North, South Korea was entirely dependent on U.S. intelligence. <<> But now, the situation has completely changed. <<> South Korea currently operates five independent military reconnaissance satellites capable of checking the Korean Peninsula every two hours. If 30 to 40 additional micro-satellites are successfully launched and operate complementarily with the reconnaissance satellites, it will enable near real-time monitoring of threats from North Korean forces, such as mobile missile launchers. The South Korean military has already deployed four Global Hawk high-altitude reconnaissance drones from the U.S. to monitor North Korea. In April, the first production unit of a domestic strategic-grade UAV, a medium-altitude reconnaissance drone, was delivered. This drone flies at an altitude of over 10 km and monitors ground targets in real time. Lee Seong-chun, a professor emeritus at Dongguk University's Department of North Korean Studies and former director of the Ministry of National Defense's Military Compilation Research Institute, stated, "Our military possesses the capabilities needed to exercise OPCON." <<> In terms of precision strike capabilities, the South Korean military has secured missiles such as Hyunmoo-2, Hyunmoo-3, Hyunmoo-4, and Hyunmoo-5, as well as the long-range air-to-ground missile Taurus. The Hyunmoo-5, deployed to front-line units starting late last year, is a high-power ballistic missile with a warhead weight of about 8 tons, designed to destroy North Korea's underground bunkers. It is considered a key weapon for completing the massive retaliation component of the South Korean three-axis system (Kill Chain – Korean Air and Missile Defense – Massive Punishment and Retaliation) to counter North Korea's nuclear and missile threats. For command and control (C2), the South Korean military operates a battlefield management system that integrates military information management systems like MIMS based on the Joint Command and Control System (KJCCS). <<> Minister An Kyu-baek met with U.S. House and Senate members at the Singapore Asia Security Summit on the 31st of last month and stated, "We fully explained our capabilities, including the fact that South Korea and the U.S. agreed that 94% of the conditions for OPCON transfer as of 2020 have already been met." A senior government official explained, "Based on the criteria agreed upon in 2014, South Korea has already achieved independent operational capabilities in ISR, precision strike, and C2," adding, "These capabilities secured by the South Korean military are those that military powers with strong economies and technologies, such as the U.S., UK, France, and Israel, can possess." <<> Some within the U.S. and South Korean militaries argue that the conditions for OPCON transfer should be revised and supplemented in response to changes in warfare, such as the increased threat from drones, and North Korea's development of new weapons like hypersonic missiles. The rationale is that the South Korean military lacks the ability to counter drones, and North Korea is highly likely to fire a mix of super-large multiple rocket launchers, short-range missiles, various cruise missiles, and hypersonic missiles, necessitating the reinforcement of air defense networks. Some retired and active-duty generals claim that South Korea must possess the same hardware and software as the U.S. military to exercise OPCON, arguing that the transfer is premature. <<> However, critics point out that if conditions continue to change, the OPCON transfer will have no set date. <<> Kim Jeong-sup, a senior research fellow at the Sejong Institute, said, "When President Roh Tae-woo pledged to retake OPCON in his 1987 presidential campaign, there were arguments that it was premature. Nearly 40 years later, despite significant improvements in our military capabilities, the same arguments persist. The transfer of OPCON should be seen not as a matter of conditions or capabilities, but as a matter of will and a policy choice." <<> Reporter Kwon Hyuk-chul nura@hani.co.kr (안규백 국방부 장관은 지난달 26일 경남 창원시 진해구에서 이재명 대통령이 참석한 가운데 열린 제1회 미래국방전략위원회에서 “내일 전시작전통제권(전작권)이 회수되더라도 우리가 스스로 지키는 데는 크게 문제가 없다”고 말했다. 이에 이 대통령이 “크게 문제가 없는 게 아니라 ‘아무 문제가 없다’라고 해야 맞겠죠”라고 하자 안 장관은 “아무 문제가 없다”고 답했다. 전작권 환수는 군사주권을 회복하고, 유사시 전쟁을 스스로 수행하는 능력을 지닌다는 의미를 띤다.)

item.title: Park Jie-won: “Song Young-gil Told President Lee His Intention to Run for Party Leadership… He Said the President Told Him to Do Well” (박지원 “송영길, 이 대통령에 당대표 출마 뜻 밝혀…잘하라고 했다더라”)
item.description:
Amid reports that lawmaker Song Young-gil, a potential candidate for the Democratic Party’s August national convention, had a private dinner with President Lee Jae-myung on the 18th, Democratic Party lawmaker Park Jie-won stated, “Song told President Lee about his decision to run for the party leadership election.” (더불어민주당 8월 전당대회 출마 가능성이 거론되는 송영길 의원이 지난 18일 이재명 대통령과 비공개 만찬을 한 가운데, 박지원 민주당 의원은 “송 의원이 이 대통령에게 전당대회 출마 결심을 얘기했다”고 전했다.)

Appearing on CBS Radio’s “Park Sung-tae’s News Show” on the 24th, Park revealed details of his phone conversation with Song the previous day. (박 의원은 24일 시비에스(CBS) 라디오 ‘박성태의 뉴스쇼’에 나와 전날 송 의원과 나눈 통화 내용을 밝혔다.)

Park said, “When I asked (at the dinner) ‘Did you bring up the party convention matter?’, (Song) said he did discuss the convention, and he told (President Lee) that he would enter a three-way race, eventually unify with Prime Minister Kim Min-seok, and create a situation where votes coalesce in the runoff.” (박 의원은 “(만찬 자리에서) ‘전당대회 관계(된 주제)는 얘기 안 했느냐’ 했더니, (송 의원은) 전당대회 관계 얘기를 했고 자기가 3자 구도로 가서 결국 김민석 총리와 단일화하는 방안을, 또 결선 투표에서 모아지는 결과를 만들어내겠다, 이런 얘기를 드렸다고 그랬다”고 전했다.)

Park added, “Then I asked, ‘What did the President say?’, and (Song replied) the President showed a positive reaction, effectively telling him to do well.” He continued, “Given that if Representative Jeong Cheong-rae enters (the convention), (Song) would enter to unify the ‘pro-Myung’ faction in a three-way race and then unify in the runoff, the nuance makes one think that Song could potentially become the party leader.” (이어 박 의원은 “‘그래서 대통령께서 뭐라고 하시더냐?’ 그랬더니 긍정적 반응을 보인 것으로, 잘하라고 이런 것으로 말씀을 했다(고 송 의원이 답했다)”고도 했다. 그러면서 “정청래 대표가 (전당대회에) 나가면 자기(송 의원)가 그렇게 나가서 3자 구도로 ‘친명’을 단일화시키고, 또 결선 투표에서 단일화하겠다 하는 걸 보면, 뉘앙스가 만약 그러다가 송 대표가 당 대표가 될 수도 있겠구나, 이런 생각도 들게 했다”고 덧붙였다.)

Earlier, Song had dinner with President Lee at the presidential residence in Hannam-dong, Seoul, on the 18th. Song, a five-term lawmaker who served in Gyeyang-gu, Incheon, resigned his seat to run for Seoul mayor in 2022, and President Lee—then the party’s senior advisor—ran and won the by-election for the same Incheon Gyeyang-gu district. (앞서 송 의원은 지난 18일 서울 한남동 대통령 관저에서 이 대통령과 저녁 식사를 함께했다. 인천 계양을에서 5선을 지낸 송 의원은 2022년 서울시장 선거 출마를 위해 의원직을 내려놓았고 당시 민주당 상임고문이었던 이 대통령이 인천 계양을 보궐선거에 출마해 당선된 바 있다.)

The upcoming Democratic Party leadership election in August is widely expected to be a three-way race among Representative Jeong Cheong-rae, Prime Minister Kim Min-seok, and Song. There are many predictions around the party that a “Song Young-gil and Kim Min-seok” united front will form against Jeong. Song has repeatedly stated that he will watch Jeong’s decision on whether to run before finalizing his own candidacy. (오는 8월 열릴 민주당 당대표 선거는 정청래 대표, 김민석 국무총리, 송 의원 3파전으로 치러질 수 있다는 관측에 무게가 실리고 있다. 당 주변에서는 정 대표에 맞서는 ‘송영길-김민석’ 연합 전선이 형성될 것이라는 전망이 많다. 송 의원은 정 대표 출마 여부를 지켜본 뒤 자신의 출마 여부를 최종적으로 결정하겠다는 의사를 여러 차례 밝힌 바 있다.)

Reporter Jeon Gwang-jun light@hani.co.kr (전광준 기자 light@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Park Yong-jin: "In Yo-han is too irresponsible" Park Ji-won: "Should have made an apology to the public" (박용진 “인요한, 너무 무책임” 박지원 “대국민 사과 했어야”)
item.description:
Criticism is mounting from the conservative bloc over the election of former People Power Party lawmaker In Yo-han as chairman of the Korean Red Cross, a public institution under the Ministry of Health and Welfare. <<> Park Yong-jin, deputy chairperson of the Regulatory Reform Committee under the President, said on the 24th regarding this appointment: "A person who acted irresponsibly as the head of the Korean Red Cross—what is this? I found it puzzling." <<> Deputy Chair Park appeared on KBS Radio's "Full Interview" that day and stated: "Former lawmaker In Yo-han has never verbally stated or criticized that he disagreed with the December 3 martial law order; rather, I got the feeling he sided with it. Some interpret his sudden resignation from his legislative seat as a form of criticism, but as someone who held a constitutional office, this is extremely irresponsible." He further criticized: "What the public wanted at that time was not for him to quit his post, but to rally efforts to end the state of insurrection early. Instead, he just fled irresponsibly." <<> Park Ji-won, a five-term lawmaker of the Democratic Party of Korea, also appeared on CBS Radio's "Park Seong-tae's News Show" that day and said: "I believe (Chairman In Yo-han) defended and led the insurrectionary forces. He should have made an apology to the public." The lawmaker added: "There are discussions about whether it was truly necessary to appoint him, especially amid the extreme situation among the conservative base." <<> Former lawmaker In, regarding former President Yoon Seok-yeol who declared martial law on December 3, expressed: "I understand him emotionally," abstained from the impeachment vote, and blamed the opposition, saying things like "If it were the old Kim Dae-jung's opposition party, they would have embraced him," defending martial law before resigning his legislative seat on December 11 last year, stating, "I will return to my primary duty to contribute to national unity and development." <<> Reporter Lee Ji-eun jieuny@hani.co.kr (인요한 전 국민의힘 의원이 보건복지부 산하 공공기관인 대한적십자사 회장으로 선출된 것을 두고 여권에서 비판이 이어지고 있다.)

item.title: [Breaking] Jeong Cheong-rae Resigns as Democratic Party Leader ([속보] 정청래, 민주당 대표직 사퇴)
item.description:
Jeong Cheong-rae, the leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, resigned from his position as party leader on the 24th. This appears to be a move to run for re-election in the upcoming party convention. (정청래 더불어민주당 대표가 24일 대표직을 사퇴했다. 전당대회에 출마하며 연임에 도전하기 위한 것으로 보인다.)

Jeong said at the conclusion of the Supreme Council meeting that morning, "I am stepping down from the party leadership today." (정 대표는 이날 오전 최고위원회의를 마치며 “저는 오늘 당 대표직을 내려 놓는다”라고 말했다.)

This approach is similar to that of President Lee Jae-myung two years ago, when he signaled his intention to seek re-election as Democratic Party leader two days before the formation of the party convention preparation committee. At that time, President Lee held a separate press conference after the Supreme Council meeting to announce his resignation from the party leadership, stating, "If I had definitively decided not to run (in the party convention), I would not have resigned." Jeong appears to have followed President Lee's precedent in his resignation. (2년 전 같은 날 이재명 대통령이 전당대회준비위원회 구성 이틀 앞두고 민주당 대표직 연임의 뜻을 내비친 것과 유사한 방식이다. 당시 이 대통령은 최고위원회의를 마치고 별도의 기자회견을 열어 대표직에서 물러나겠다고 밝히며 “아무래도 (전당대회에) 출마하지 않겠다고 확정했다면 사퇴하지 않았을 것”이라고 발언했다. 정 대표도 이 대통령의 전례를 따라 사퇴한 것으로 보인다.)
